summary: This article explains how tiny coral polyps build reefs, how reefs turn into islands like the Farasan Islands, why corals need sunlight and clean water, and how heat can harm them.
introduce: Read the title “Coral Islands of the Red Sea” aloud and ask each student to write one question they hope the article will answer. Collect a few questions, then explain that today they will find the one big idea that ties all the details together.

keyTerms.def: a tiny, soft sea animal that builds coral
a hard, pale rock made mostly from shells and skeletons of sea animals
very small plant-like living things that make food from sunlight

challengeTerms.def: a close relationship between two different living things that often helps both
the variety of different living things in a place
sand, mud, or small pieces of material that settle in water

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that tiny animals can build something as big as an island? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain how living things and the ocean work together to build a coral island.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review polyp, limestone, and algae, and let weak readers complete a main-idea-and-details web with a partner.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses symbiosis, biodiversity, and sediment to state the main idea of the article in their own words.
